golden.flac provenance record
==============================

Produced by:
  tools/venv/.venv/bin/python3 internal/engine/tagio/testdata/gen_golden_flac.py

Pinned versions (tools/venv/requirements.txt, confirmed at generation time):
  beets      2.13.1
  mediafile  0.17.0
  mutagen    1.48.1 (vendor string, confirmed on the golden's own
             VORBIS_COMMENT block: "Mutagen 1.48.1")

Starting point: internal/harness/oracle/testdata/template.flac, the
committed 42-byte tag-free STREAMINFO-only container, copied to a
scratch path before any write. The script reads that path at
generation time only; golden.flac is thereafter self-contained
(Resolution R3).

Declared input (INPUT in gen_golden_flac.py, restated field by field;
this is the input, not the emitted comment set -- nothing below
reconstructs it from golden.flac's bytes)
-------------------------------------------------------------------

INV:409-427's own shape, restated:
  album          = "Al"
  albumartists   = ["X", "Y"]
  artist         = "A"
  bpm            = 120

  disc           = 1
  disctotal      = 2
  title          = "T"
  track          = 3
  tracktotal     = 12
  albumtype      = "album"
  albumtypes     = ["album", "live"]

The four corpus-unreachable cases a mediafile write can express:
  year           = 0        (the zero year)
  original_year  = 0        (the zero year, second date field)
  arrangers      = []       (the empty list)
  catalognum     = ""       (empty; C5's read-only-trailing-style pair)
  barcode        = ""       (empty; C5's other read-only-trailing-style pair)

Task 8's sixteen ledger-silent keys, each given a real value:
  acoustid_fingerprint = "invented-fingerprint-value"
  acoustid_id           = "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555"
  comments              = "Invented comment text."
  encoder               = "Invented Encoder 1.0"
  genres                = ["Ambient", "Drone"]
  grouping              = "Invented Grouping"

  lyrics                = "la la la"

  rg_track_gain         = -7.25

Plus one picture, added after MediaFile.update via mf.images = [Image(...)]:
  data = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + b"invented-picture-payload" (32 bytes)
  desc = "cover"
  type = ImageType.front (APIC index 3)
This is a small invented blob with a sniffable PNG magic prefix, not a
decodable image; 8a asserts nothing about it beyond its block
surviving a parse (8b grades it).

Cases the record names as expressible-but-not-included: none. Every
rule this task lists as reachable through a mediafile write is
present above.

Two cases stay out of INPUT by construction, and are Task 8's
hand-built cases instead:
  - An invalid-UTF-8 byte sequence: mediafile writes valid UTF-8 only,
    so no value it accepts can carry one.
  - A U+007E comment field name: mutagen's is_valid_key
    (mutagen/_vorbis.py:25-41) refuses any name above 0x7D, so
    mediafile's own write path cannot reach it.

Read-back of the four corpus-unreachable cases, confirmed against the
committed golden.flac (mediafile.MediaFile, same pinned venv):
  year           -> 0, month -> None, day -> None
  original_year  -> 0, original_month -> None, original_day -> None
  arrangers      -> None (empty on disk reads back indistinguishable
                    from absent, per C2)
  catalognum     -> None (CATALOGNUMBER="" is on disk; the read-only
                    trailing styles CATALOGID and DISCOGS_CATALOG make
                    the last-applicable-style read return absent, C5)
  barcode        -> None (BARCODE="" is on disk; the read-only
                    trailing styles UPC, EAN/UPN, EAN and UPN make the
                    last-applicable-style read return absent, C5)

golden.flac
-----------

Size: 2216 bytes (well under 10 KiB).

Decoded block chain, in on-disk order (type, last-block flag, declared
payload length in bytes, not counting the 4-byte block header):

  0  STREAMINFO      type=0  last=false  declared_len=34
  1  VORBIS_COMMENT  type=4  last=false  declared_len=1060
  2  PICTURE         type=6  last=false  declared_len=78
  3  PADDING         type=1  last=true   declared_len=1024

Total metadata region: 4 (signature) + (4+34) + (4+1060) + (4+78) +
(4+1024) = 2216 bytes, matching the file size exactly: the frame
region's offset is 2216 and its length is 0 (the template is silent,
carries zero audio samples, and this script never adds any).

VORBIS_COMMENT is written immediately after STREAMINFO, as C9a states
a freshly created block always is. This chain does not contradict
C9a.

Vendor string (verbatim): "Mutagen 1.48.1"

Decoded comment sequence, in on-disk order (this is what Task 7
implements to):

  TITLE=T
  TRACK=3
  TRACKNUMBER=3
  TRACKTOTAL=12
  TRACKC=12
  TOTALTRACKS=12

This sequence matches this plan's hypothesis: sorted_fields order
first (with DateItemField names sorted as date0/date1/date2, which is
why DATE/YEAR lands between COMPILATION and DISC rather than near the
end of the alphabet, and why ORIGINALDATE lands near "original_year"'s
own alphabetical position), then style declaration order within a
field (RELEASETYPE before MUSICBRAINZ_ALBUMTYPE, ALBUMARTISTS before
ALBUM_ARTISTS, DESCRIPTION before COMMENT, and so on), then list order
within a style (X before Y, album before live, Ambient before Drone).
The albumtype/albumtypes collision confirms the plural-wins rule
(C3): albumtype writes RELEASETYPE=[album] and
MUSICBRAINZ_ALBUMTYPE=[album] first (its comments sort earlier,
alphabetically before "albumtypes"), then albumtypes overwrites both
keys' values in place to the two-element list, without moving their
position in the block. No mismatch to report.

PICTURE block payload, decoded (mutagen.flac.Picture):
  type  = 3 (front cover, APIC index)
  mime  = "image/png" (sniffed from the data's magic prefix)
  desc  = "cover"
  width, height, depth, colors = 0, 0, 0, 0 (mediafile's FLAC image
          write always emits zero geometry; see spec's PICTURE
          section)
  data length = 32 bytes, prefix \x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n

gitleaks: golden.flac was not flagged by a local gitleaks run over the
tracked worktree; .gitleaksignore is unchanged.
